description: q-Collatz divergence-half probe: forward-orbit classification of the Skein-Collatz map from positive Laurent seeds. Exact ℤ[q^±1] arithmetic. Exploratory research probe (NOT canonical production).
findings: The map's domain {P : P(-1) ∈ {0,-1}} is NOT forward-invariant: 6042/6045 positive Laurent seeds leave the domain (C_q undefined at some iterate), 5369 of them after a single step; max in-domain prefix before escape = 4.

No divergent orbit and no rogue cycle found: all non-escaping orbits reach the fundamental 2-cycle {q^-1, 1+q^-1}. The only convergents are the cycle elements and backward-tree preimages (e.g. q+2+q^-1 -> 1+q^-1).

Structural consequence for conj:q-collatz: the convergence claim 'for all P in ℤ[q^±1]_{>0}' is ill-posed on the naive positive cone (C_q is undefined on ~all of it). The correct hypothesis is the DOMAIN-STABLE cone — elements whose entire forward orbit stays in {P(-1) ∈ {0,-1}} — a Cantor-thin set (the backward orbit of the cycle). This partiality has NO classical analog: over ℤ every integer is even or odd, so the domain is everything.
scope: Bounded forward probe (window q^-3..q^5, coeffs 0..2, 400 steps). Evidence for domain non-invariance + absence of divergence in this family; NOT a proof.
